title: They didn’t clap.
paragraphs:
Because this wasn’t goodbye…
this felt like something bigger.

Not slowly fading into legend…
not dissolving into metaphor…
And here’s the part we don’t talk about enough—

These were the same men who doubted Him.
The same voices that argued about who was greatest.
The same feet that ran when the cross got heavy.

They’re staring into the sky…
faces cracked open with awe…
hearts trembling between fear and wonder.
If He really just ascended like that…
Then everything He said is true.
And if everything He said is true…
Then nothing in their lives could stay the same.
We love the idea of Jesus…

We like grace…
but we resist surrender.

We celebrate resurrection…
but ignore His authority.
And that’s where the tension lives.
Because the ascension isn’t just a beautiful moment.
Jesus is not just risen—He is reigning.

“He was taken up before their very eyes, and a cloud hid Him from their sight.
They were looking intently up into the sky as He was going, when suddenly two men dressed in white stood beside them.
‘Men of Galilee,’ they said, ‘why do you stand here looking into the sky? This same Jesus… will come back in the same way you have seen Him go into heaven.’”

Not a softer version.
Not a symbolic return.
Not a revised message.

The One who called out sin.
The One who touched lepers.
The One who flipped tables.
The One who carried a cross meant for you.

Some scholars interpret the “cloud” not just as weather…
but as a manifestation of God’s glory—like the cloud in Exodus that led Israel.
And here’s where it gets uncomfortable.
then your secret life is not hidden.

That habit you excuse?
He sees it.

That pride you protect?
He opposes it.
That sin you renamed to make it feel lighter?
The same Jesus who sees everything…
“But God demonstrates His own love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”

Not when you cleaned up.
Not when you got consistent.
Not when you fixed your image.
While you were still in it.

Still hiding.
Still failing.
Still pretending.
“Repent, then, and turn to God, so that your sins may be wiped out…”

They want forgiveness…
but not transformation.

They want heaven…
but not holiness.

Jesus didn’t just rise to inspire you.
He reigns to command you.
He rules with a scarred body.
He intercedes for you even now.
“He is able to save completely those who come to God through Him, because He always lives to intercede for them.”

Jesus is alive…
seated in authority…
and speaking your name before the Father.
So what will you do with that?
Keep negotiating with a God who already gave everything?
Or will you finally look up…

The King has ascended.
And He is coming back.
Run to Jesus—not away from Him.
Because the same sky that received Him…
you won’t want to be pretending.
If this pierced something in you… don’t ignore it.
